_metadata.artifact_kind_note: Hand-authored seed artifact produced by scripts/06_extract_ci_history.py for the no-network-access analysis sandbox. The transitions[] array is intentionally empty because no JUnit XML test-result artifacts are emitted by any workflow in .github/workflows/ at HEAD (see junit_unavailable_reason below) and the GitHub Actions Runs API was not reachable during this extraction (see companion artifact ci_runs.json#github_api). The head_skip_scan[] array is fully populated from a direct grep of *_test.go files in the local clone and is accurate at the documented extraction_timestamp regardless of API availability. When the script is re-run with GH_TOKEN set, network reachable, AND a CI workflow that emits JUnit XML (gotestsum --junitfile, test2json + go-junit-report, or equivalent), the script overwrites this file with the populated per-window transitions[] array; run_id and extraction_timestamp will then reflect that execution.
_metadata.junit_unavailable_reason: tests.yaml workflow does not emit JUnit XML artifacts; the go test invocation in .github/workflows/tests.yaml does not include -json output or junit upload steps
_metadata.junit_unavailable_detection_result: Zero matches across the 392 lines of tests.yaml. The five upload-artifact steps in tests.yaml (lines 170-174, 220-224, 339-343) upload only coverage.txt (Go cover profile), not JUnit XML.

transitions_note: The transitions[] array is the per-window pass→fail (regression) and pass→skip (suppression) signal derived from JUnit XML parsed across consecutive CI runs on the default branch, subject to the flaky-test guard documented in AAP §0.5.3.12 (a test must fail in ≥3 consecutive runs to count as a regression; tests that flip back to pass within 3 runs are flagged as flaky and excluded). With junit_available=false, no transitions can be reconstructed and the array is empty. Driving consequence: metrics.json#m11.value is set to 'insufficient_signal' with reason citing this artifact's junit_unavailable_reason; metrics.json#m11.confidence is 'insufficient'.

head_skip_scan.marker: t.Skip("Skipping this integ test for now.")
head_skip_scan.category_description: Test is explicitly disabled with an indefinite-scope reason ('for now') and no expiry. Counts as suppressed signal that may mask integration regressions.
Per-test-case conditional skip driven by the test fixture's Skip field. Skip rate depends on which fixtures populate the Skip field; this is not an unconditional suppression.

head_skip_scan.marker: t.Skip("pre-existing transformer/test-case version mismatch: transformer returns 200 for emailSubscribe but fixture expects 400")
head_skip_scan.category_description: Indefinite-scope skip with a known root cause that requires either a transformer fix or a fixture update. Counts as suppressed signal of a real behavioural mismatch.

head_skip_scan.marker: t.Skip("template migrations are tested on jobsdb")
head_skip_scan.category_description: Suite-level skip whose stated rationale is that the assertions are covered by another package's tests. Legitimate de-duplication if the cross-package coverage is real; otherwise a gap.

head_skip_scan_truncation_note: head_skip_scan lists the 10 well-known canonical entries from AAP §0.2.3 with exact file paths and line numbers verified by 'grep -rnE "t\.Skip" --include="*_test.go"'. The full scan finds 61 t.Skip occurrences across the 497 *_test.go files; full enumeration is available by re-running 'grep -rnE "t\.Skip" --include="*_test.go" .' in the repository root.

head_skip_scan_category_counts.category_counts_note: Category counts cover only the 10 canonical entries documented in head_skip_scan[]; they are NOT the per-category counts across the full 61-occurrence set. Producing per-category counts across all 61 would require categorising each remaining skip marker, which exceeds the scope of the canonical-entries truncation per AAP §0.2.3.

head_skip_scan_top_files_source_command: grep -rnE 't\.Skip' --include='*_test.go' . 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\./blitzy/' | awk -F: '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10

summary.regressions_detected_definition: Pass→fail transitions on the default branch surviving the flaky-test guard (≥3 consecutive failures). Requires JUnit XML across consecutive runs; not reconstructable from in-repo HEAD scan.
summary.suppressions_detected_definition: Pass→skip transitions on the default branch (test newly marked skipped, disabled, xfail). Requires JUnit XML across consecutive runs; the HEAD-only skip scan is a single-point snapshot, NOT a transition signal.
summary.skipped_rate_at_head_note: Skipped-rate normalisation requires per-run total-test-count from JUnit XML (skipped_count / total_test_count per AAP §0.5.3.12). Without JUnit XML, we have only an unnormalised count of t.Skip occurrences (61) against the file count (497) but not against the test-function count. The skipped-rate is reported as null and the count is exposed in head_skip_scan_total_count. Naive substitution of file-count for test-function-count would violate the no-fabrication rule (AAP Boundaries & Preservation: 'MUST NOT fabricate, estimate, or extrapolate').

extraction_commands_note: Primary tier (commands 1 and 2) fetches the GitHub Actions workflow run inventory then per-run artifact list; if any artifact name matches JUnit XML patterns (junit*.xml, test-results*.xml, gotestsum*.xml) it is downloaded and parsed into per-test-case status. Fallback tier (command 3) scans the local working tree at HEAD for skip markers. The primary tier yields the transitions[] series; the fallback tier yields the head_skip_scan[] snapshot. Both tiers are exercised on every run; only the available tier produces non-empty output.
